info.title: Nano — Document Extraction External Agent API
info.description:
Pull queue for an external agent that turns uploaded health documents (体检报告 PDFs, photographed paper lab printouts, discharge summaries) into structured digital-twin data.

Every response is HTTP 200 with a JSON body, INCLUDING routine failures — branch on `reason`, never on a status code.

Separate service from the Viva AG API (`/viva-ag/*`): different token, different queue, no shared state. The prose contract, which is the authoritative one, is served at `GET /doc-extract/docs`.

tags.name: discovery
tags.description: Version handshake, the contract, and the extraction vocabulary

tags.name: testing
tags.description: Dry-run against the real validator, with no job and no write

get.description: The authoritative document. Read this first — it is written to be sufficient on its own.

Every biomarker nano can store, generated live from biomarker_catalog. A `key_name` outside this list is NOT accepted — send it in `unmapped` instead, never mapped onto a neighbouring marker. The same list ships with every claim; this endpoint exists so a prompt can be built and tuned before any job exists.

post.summary: Dry-run a result payload against the real validator
post.description: Runs the SAME pure validator the result path runs, with no job, no claim and no write. `job_uid` and `result_token` are ignored. Iterate here until `rejected` is empty before running a live job.

post.summary: Claim the head of the queue
post.description: Atomic (FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED): two pollers get two different jobs, never the same one twice. An empty queue is `{"success":true,"job":null}` — not an error. Mints a fresh `result_token` and invalidates any previous holder's.
Extends from now. Send one at least every `lease_seconds / 2`, from a separate timer rather than between processing steps.

result_token.description: Or send it as the X-Doc-Extract-Job-Token header

post.description:
Validated then written: document metadata, the lab panel (as health_reports + health_events), findings (as personal memory facts), then one digital-twin refresh.

Nano REJECTS, never repairs — a rejected entry is not written, the rest of the submission still lands, and every refusal comes back in `rejected` with a reason. Always read it: it is the only signal that an extraction is systematically wrong.

Idempotent: a repeat with the same token returns `already_completed` and writes nothing.

report_id.description: null when no observations were stored — see the missing_date rule

post.description: `retryable: false` for anything a retry cannot fix — an encrypted PDF, a blank scan, a photo of something that is not a health document. A document with nothing extractable is NOT a failure: submit a result with metadata and a summary instead.

serviceToken.description: DOC_EXTRACT_API_TOKEN, minted as `dex_` + 32 hex. Issued per environment; the two are never interchangeable.

jobToken.name: X-Doc-Extract-Job-Token
jobToken.description: The per-job fencing token from the claim. Rotated on every claim, so a stale one means the lease moved on. Never sent as a query parameter — query strings land in access logs and this gates a medical record.

key_name.description: Use verbatim. The only identifier nano resolves.

unit.description: The unit values are stored in. Send the report's own unit; nano converts only the documented pairs.

ref_high.description: Nano's reference value, given for sanity-checking. Some are risk thresholds rather than physiological ceilings.

url.description: Presigned, direct from object storage. Bytes never pass through nano.

supports_range.description: HTTP Range works — chunk or resume a large file

DocType.description: On a claimed job this is almost always "other": no client asks the user to classify an upload, so filling it in is part of the extraction.

subject.description: Enough to read an age- or sex-dependent reference range, and nothing more. Carries no user id, name or contact of any kind; `ref` is the job_uid.

language.description: Write `summary` and finding `text` in this language

key_name.description: From the catalog, verbatim. Anything else belongs in `unmapped`.

value.description: A number — not a range, not "<0.5", not a string carrying the unit

unit.description: As printed on the report. Case, spacing and µ/u are normalised.

source_text.description: The line it was read from. Not stored as data — it is what makes a wrong read diagnosable.

Finding.description: A durable personal fact the document asserts about the patient. These filter what products may be recommended and feed nutrition formulation, so a wrongly recorded allergy is worse than a missed one. Not a drug the report merely mentions, not a condition it rules out, not family history.

confidence.description: Required. Below 0.8 is rejected, and an absent confidence is rejected outright.

Unmapped.description: An analyte read off the report that is not in the catalog. Expected and useful — a real 体检报告 carries 50-80 analytes and nano models 25. This is how the catalog gets extended.

ResultPayload.description: Every field but job_uid and result_token is optional. A document with nothing extractable is still a legitimate result — send metadata and a summary with empty arrays rather than calling /jobs/fail.

doc_date.description: The date ON the report. Never today's date as a stand-in — a wrong date puts an old panel into the twin as though it were current.

summary.description: Plain language, in the subject's language. No ':::' — those are display-card fences in nano's chat renderer and are stripped on ingest.
